**Purpose and approach.** Chesapeake says it uses derivatives to reduce exposure to commodity price swings and to protect expected operating cash flow [1]. In its market risk disclosure it says it enters into derivative instruments to mitigate a portion of its exposure to adverse price changes [2]. It also acknowledges that these arrangements may limit the benefit it would receive from higher commodity prices [3].

**Valuation.** It determines fair value using established index prices, volatility curves and discount factors, and compares those estimates to counterparty valuations for reasonableness [4].

**Counterparty non-performance risk.** Non-performance risk is considered in the valuation of the derivatives, and to date it has not had a material impact on their values [5]. Chesapeake mitigates counterparty risk by contracting only with highly rated counterparties or those it deems to have acceptable credit strength [6]. Its derivative instruments were spread among 7 counterparties at year-end [7]. Its hedging arrangements also require counterparties to post collateral if their obligations to it exceed defined thresholds [8].
